Checkpoints of the out-of-bag path

Source: R/oob_path.R
oob_path_checkpoints.Rd

The numbers of splits at which rpf() with oob_path = TRUE evaluates the out-of-bag (OOB) error: a geometric grid with four points per doubling, round(25 * 2^(j / 4)) from 6 up to n_splits (it contains 12, 25, 50, ..., 1600, 3200), and n_splits itself; every number up to 12 if n_splits <= 12. The error changes slowly in log(n_splits), so a geometric grid resolves it evenly, and the path's memory, 2 * nrow(x) * length(checkpoints) doubles, stays small; every split would cost 2 * nrow(x) * n_splits.

Usage

oob_path_checkpoints(n_splits, ...)

Arguments

n_splits

[integer(1)]: The largest number of splits (the n_splits of the fit). Was splits.

...

Only the old name splits, deprecated: it works, with a warning.

Value

An increasing integer vector.

See also

rpf() (oob_path)

Examples

oob_path_checkpoints(400)
#>  [1]   6   7   9  11  12  15  18  21  25  30  35  42  50  59  71  84 100 119 141
#> [20] 168 200 238 283 336 400
